title: 𓂋𓄿 𓏌𓅱 𓉐𓂋𓏏𓂻 𓅓 𓉔𓂋𓅱𓇳
titleEn: Book of the Dead of Ani — Spell 17, part 5
part: Spell 17, part 5 — Khepri in his bark, the keepers, and the meal of faience (Plate 10)
work: Book of the Dead of Ani
workEn: Book of the Dead of Ani
draftNote: Draft — the hieroglyphs are read from the printed type of Budge's 1895 edition of the papyrus, and the signs and readings are still being checked; expect changes.
source: Papyrus of Ani (British Museum EA 10470), Plate X. Hieroglyphs transcribed from the interlinear text of E. A. W. Budge, The Book of the Dead: The Papyrus of Ani in the British Museum (London, 1895), pp. 52–53; Budge's transliteration and word-by-word English were used to check the reading of the signs and the sense, never for wording. Only the papyrus's own text is given: the passages Budge supplies from other papyri in his appendixes and footnotes are left out. Transliteration in the Leiden convention, with the reed written i; translation made fresh from the Egyptian. Shown left to right; the papyrus is written in columns read from the top down. The line under each word ("say") is the conventional Egyptological classroom pronunciation — a neutral e between consonants; ꜣ and ꜥ as a; w as u or w; ṯ as tj; ḏ as dj; ḫ and ẖ as kh; š as sh — an artificial teaching pronunciation, since the vowels of Egyptian were never written. The grouping of signs within a word follows Budge's type, which regularises the scribe's hand.
about: The fifth part of Spell 17 ends Ani's plea to Khepri and explains it: the god in his bark is Ra himself, the keepers who inspect are Isis and Nephthys, the abominations of the gods are filth(?) and lying, and Anubis keeps watch over the chest that holds the innards(?) of Osiris. The evening meal of faience brought in Tanenet is given three readings in turn, among them the sky and the earth and the Eye of Horus. A new statement then speaks of the house that Atum built and of Ani, who has come into this land and is Atum. On the papyrus it runs over Plate 10, lines 122 to 132.

sentences.l: was-brought · to-him · an-evening-meal · of · faience · which-is-in · Tanenet
sentences.i: An evening meal of faience, which is in Tanenet, was brought to him.
sentences.n: Budge's group àn-nef is split here into in and n·f. in 'was brought' is the jar on legs (coded W25, approximate; the type shows a small ring on a narrow two-legged body), the sign that writes ini 'bring', with water n as its complement: taken as the passive sḏm, 'was brought', with n·f 'to him', water n and ·f. It could also be the sḏm·n·f in·n·f 'he has brought'; but the gloss in line 126 quotes the statement as rdyt n·f, 'was given to him', which points to the passive. The papyrus writes msyt m ṯḥnt in red. msyt is the three skins ms with s and two reeds, with a table (coded R3, approximate; a flat top on a short stem), a loaf (coded X4, approximate) and plural strokes as classifiers: taken as msyt 'evening meal', the meal laid on the table (Budge: mesi); its t is not written here, but it is in line 126. m 'of' names what the meal is made of. ṯḥnt 'faience' is the tethering rope ṯ, the wick ḥ, n and t, with the bead collar (coded S15, approximate) and three grains: the gleaming glazed ware (Budge: θeḥent, which he takes for a plant). imt 'which is in' is the nisba imy in its feminine form, agreeing with msyt. tꜣnnt is t with the kiln tꜣ (U30, approximate), a long hatched bar (coded X4, approximate; perhaps the strip of land) and a stroke, then the rush twice with n twice as complement, t and the house sign: Tanenet, a holy place (Budge: Tanenet); where it lay is not clear. Both readings are the best the signs give, but neither is sure: a meal 'of faience' is strange, and Budge takes ṯḥnt for a plant (saffron); it is the bead-collar sign, if it is rightly read, and the grains, the classifier of minerals, that point to the glazed ware. These words end the plea to Khepri begun in line 116; the gloss in line 126 names 'him' as Osiris.

sentences.i: Khepri in the midst of his bark: it is Ra himself.
sentences.n: The answer repeats the name and title of line 116 and explains them with a noun and pw: rꜥ pw 'it is Ra'. ḫpri is the scarab ḫpr with r, i and a god; ḥry-ib has the face with its stroke and the heart; wiꜣ·f 'his bark' is written as in line 116 (the boat coded P1, approximate). rꜥ is the god with the sun on his head. ḏs·f 'himself' is the cobra ḏ and the folded cloth s, with ·f: after a noun it stresses the person, 'Ra himself'. Khepri, the sun at dawn, is Ra in one of his forms.

sentences.l: as-for · those · (of) · keepers · who-inspect · the-baboons(?) · it-is · Isis · it-is · Nephthys · it-is
sentences.i: As for those keepers who inspect, they are the baboons(?): they are Isis and Nephthys.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ir nnw n iryw sipw in red; the answer is in black. The gloss takes up 'those keepers who inspect' of line 117. nnw n iryw is the demonstrative nn joined to its noun by the genitive n, 'those (of) keepers', the classical construction; in line 117 nnw stood without n. iryw is written as there, but with a seated man (A1) where line 117 has the man holding a stick; sipw 'who inspect' is written as there, without the man. bntt is the foot b, n, t twice, a seated baboon (coded E32) and a stroke: taken as a word for the baboon in a feminine form, and the two t may mark a feminine dual, 'the two (female) baboons', which would suit the two goddesses named after it (Budge: bentet). The reading is uncertain. ꜣst 'Isis' is the seat with t and the egg (H8), the classifier of female beings; nbt-ḥwt 'Nephthys' is the enclosure with the basket on it, with a snake (coded I12, approximate; the type shows a looped body and no basket). Each noun has its own pw, 'it is …, it is …'. The two sisters of Osiris, his mourners, are here the keepers; baboons are the animals that greet the rising sun.

sentences.i: As for those abominations of the gods, they are filth(?) and falsehood.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ir nnw n bwt in red; nṯrw and the answer are in black. The gloss takes up 'those things that are the abomination of the gods' of line 121. nnw is written as in line 117 (U19 approximate), without the stroke. Budge's group en butu is kept as one word, n-bwt, because the water n is printed over the foot b: it is the genitive n after nn, as in the gloss before, and bwt 'abomination', the foot b, w and t, here with a fish (coded K1, approximate) as classifier where line 121 has the bird of bad things; the fish was a forbidden food and often classifies bwt. nṯrw is the flag three times. ḥsw is the wick ḥ, the folded cloth s and w, with a rounded lump (coded Aa2, approximate; one reader saw the sign of dung, F52) and plural strokes: taken as ḥs 'excrement, filth' (Budge: ḥesu); the reading is not sure. pw follows the first noun and covers both. grg 'falsehood' is the jar-stand g and r, which spell out the hoe grg (U17), with the bird of bad things and plural strokes, as in the weighing of the heart. Filth and lying are what the gods cannot bear and the dead man must be free of.

sentences.i: As for the one who passes the place of purification in the midst of the Meseqet, it is Anubis, who is behind the chest that holds the innards(?) of Osiris.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ir swꜣ wꜥbt ḥry-ib msqt in red. swꜣ is the crossed sticks (Z9) with walking legs, read swꜣ 'pass' as in the Spell 125 address: the participle 'who passes', with wꜥbt as its object (Budge reads seś). wꜥbt 'the place of purification' is the vase pouring water over a leg (D60), the water lines, t and the house sign, as in part 3: the place where the body was washed and embalmed. ḥry-ib is the face and the heart, without strokes. msqt as in line 121. Budge's groups em and sa are joined here as m-sꜣ 'behind', the owl m and the sign sꜣ (Aa18) with a stroke, as in part 3. iw·f m-sꜣ 'he being behind' describes Anubis: iw·f with a prepositional phrase. ꜥfdt 'the chest' is the arm ꜥ and f, a long low box (coded Q6, approximate), then t and the hand d, the t written before the d (Budge: āfṭet); Budge's numeral 126 is printed after the box. ntt 'which' is nty in its feminine form, agreeing with ꜥfdt. ẖr is the sign ẖr (T28) with r and a stroke: the preposition 'under', which also means 'carrying, holding', so that ntt ẖr is 'which holds'. mꜥẖtw is the owl m, the arm ꜥ, a sign coded as the belly ẖ (F32, approximate; a horizontal sign with a tuft at one end and an oval at the other), t and a small bird read w (it may be the vulture ꜣ), with the piece of flesh (coded F51, approximate) and plural strokes: taken as a word for the innards (Budge: māχatu); the reading is not sure. nt wsir 'of Osiris' has the genitive in its feminine form. Anubis, the god of embalming, keeps watch over the chest that holds the organs of Osiris.

sentences.i: As for the one to whom the evening meal of faience in Tanenet was given, it is Osiris.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ir rdyt n·f msyt m ṯḥnt imt tꜣnnt in red; wsir pw is in black. Budge's group erṭāit-nef is split here into rdyt and n·f. rdyt is r and the giving arm di, with two reeds, t and the roll; the arm is Budge's restoration of damage, inside his square brackets, with the r printed above them. It is taken as a passive of rdi 'give', 'was given', quoting the statement of line 122 with rdi in place of ini; the ending yt is not explained (it may be the feminine passive participle, 'what was given'). After ir the quoted words stand for the one they speak of, 'as for (the one to whom) … was given'. msyt has its t here; ṯḥnt has one grain and plural strokes; imt is written im, without the t. The answer names the 'him' of line 122: the meal of faience is brought to Osiris.

sentences.i: Another saying: as for the evening meal of faience in Tanenet, it is the sky and the earth.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ky ḏd in red, the rest in black. ky ḏd 'another saying' brings in a second explanation, as in part 1; this one explains the meal and its place, not the one who receives it. imt is written im with a stroke, without the t (Budge: àmu). pt 'sky' is p and t with the sign of the sky. tꜣ 'earth' is a flat sign with its left end curled down, small loops hanging under it and a leg at the right end (coded N16, approximate; it is not the plain earth sign of tꜣwy in line 128). pt pw tꜣ pw: 'it is the sky, it is the earth'.

sentences.l: another · saying · the-beating(?) · of-Shu · of · the-Two-Lands · it-is · in · Herakleopolis
sentences.i: Another saying: it is the beating(?) of the Two Lands by Shu, in Herakleopolis.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ky ḏd qnqn in red, šw nt in black, tꜣwy pw m in red, and nni-nsw in black. qnqn is the hill-slope q and n written twice, with the crossed sticks (Z9) and the low sign U15 as classifiers: taken as qnqn 'beat, strike', here a noun, 'the beating', with šw 'Shu' after it as the one who does it (Budge: qenqen). šw is the feather šw with w and a god. nt is the genitive in its feminine form, though qnqn is masculine; it is taken as joining the Two Lands to the beating. tꜣwy 'the Two Lands' is the earth sign with two small signs coded N21 (approximate) as classifiers. m 'in' is written with the sign Aa15. nni-nsw 'Herakleopolis' is written as in part 2, here with a small seated figure (coded A1, approximate). The whole is uncertain: the words may also be a name, 'Shu, the Beater of the Two Lands', and nt is hard to fit either way. Shu, the air, stands between the sky and the earth of the gloss before; in part 1, Herakleopolis is where Ra first appeared as king.

sentences.l: as-for · the-evening-meal · of · faience · the-Eye · of-Horus · it-is
sentences.i: As for the evening meal of faience, it is the Eye of Horus.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ir msyt m ṯḥnt irt in red; ḥr pw is in black. irt ḥr 'the Eye of Horus' is the eye with t and a stroke (Budge reads it maat), and the falcon with a god, the two nouns side by side. The meal of faience is now the Eye of Horus, which Seth tore and Thoth made whole, the model of every offering given to the dead.

sentences.l: as-for · Tanenet · the-place-of-union(?) · it-is · of · Osiris
sentences.i: As for Tanenet, it is the place of union(?) of Osiris.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes the seat twice, st wsir; read wsir. A seat (Q1) stands alone before the group wsir, and Budge prints '(sic)' over it: the scribe began the name with its seat and then wrote the whole group, so the first seat is not read. It cannot well be another word: this papyrus writes st 'seat, place' with t and the house sign, and ꜣst 'Isis' with t and the egg (as in line 124), never with the bare seat, and 'the place of union of the seat of Osiris' would be an empty phrase. The gloss is in black. tꜣnnt as before; Budge's numeral 130 is printed inside it, between the strokes and the rushes. smꜣt is the lung and windpipe smꜣ (F36) with ꜣ and t, and the roll: taken as a noun from smꜣ 'unite', 'the place of union' (Budge: samat). smꜣ-tꜣ 'join the earth' is said of burial, so the tomb of Osiris may be meant; the sense is not sure. pw stands between the noun and its genitive nt wsir, as it often does.

sentences.l: is-built · house-your · (by) · Atum · is-founded · mansion-your · (by) · the-Double-Lion
sentences.i: Your house has been built by Atum; your mansion has been founded by the Double-Lion.
sentences.n: A new statement begins, spoken to 'you'. qd 'build' is the man building a wall (A35), the sign that writes qd. In qd pr·k tm the object-like noun pr·k stands before Atum: the verb is read as the passive sḏm, 'your house is built', with the doer after it, though the preposition in 'by' is not written and is supplied, so the reading is not sure. The words could also be spoken to the gods themselves, 'your house is built, Atum'. pr·k is the house with a stroke and ·k. tm 'Atum' is t and the sledge tm (U15) with a god, as in part 1. snt is the bolt s, n and t, with a cord (coded V6, approximate) as classifier: taken as snṯ 'found, lay out (a building)', written with t for ṯ (the two had fallen together in speech, as in iṯ·n·f in line 131), in the same construction (Budge: sent). ḥwt·k 'your mansion' is the enclosure ḥwt with t, the house sign and ·k. rwti 'the Double-Lion' is the recumbent lion rw twice and a stroke, then the tethering rope ṯ, here standing for t, with i and a god (Budge: Rereθà); the Spell 125 declarations write the name with t. The Double-Lion is Shu and Tefnut, the first pair Atum made. Whose house is meant is not said.

sentences.l: has-arrived · the-remedy(?) · pure · Horus · divine(?) · Seth · and-vice-versa
sentences.i: The remedy(?) has arrived: Horus is pure and Seth is divine(?), and the other way round.
sentences.n: Budge's groups peḥ and en are joined here as pḥ·n, the sḏm·n·f of pḥ 'reach, arrive': the rump pḥ (F22) with walking legs, and n. The n could also be the preposition 'to', with no subject written. rrt is r twice (the first long and rounded; coded D21, approximate) and t, with three grains: the grains classify minerals, medicines and powders, and rrt is taken as such a substance, a word not otherwise known (Budge: rert); the scribe may have miswritten another word. twri is t and the swallow wr with r, i and the roll, twr 'be clean, pure', as in the Spell 125 address (there with the pouring vessel as a further classifier). nṯrty is the flag nṯr with r, t, two strokes y and the roll: taken as nṯri 'be divine'. Each verb stands before its noun as the predicate of a sentence of quality, 'pure is Horus, divine(?) is Seth', as a verb of quality does (nfr X 'X is good'); the endings i and ty are not explained. Read as active verbs, 'Horus purifies, Seth makes divine', both would lack an object, and 'make divine' would need the causative s-nṯr. Of the nouns, ḥr is the falcon with a god; stẖ is the bolt s and t with a plain rectangle (coded N37, approximate) read ẖ, and a god, as in part 2. ṯs-pẖr 'and the other way round', in red, is the knot ṯs (S24) and one long oblong (coded D21, approximate) with the roll; part 3 writes it with the knot and the sign pẖr. If the oblong is r, only the end of pẖr is written; one reader took it for the intestine (F48), which writes pẖr itself. The sense of the whole is uncertain: perhaps the substance makes the two rivals alike, each pure and each divine, which is what ṯs-pẖr 'and the other way round' says.

sentences.l: has-come-he · into · land · this · has-taken-(it)-he · with · two-feet-his · the-Osiris · the-scribe · Ani · true-of-voice · before · Osiris
sentences.i: He has come into this land and has taken it with his two feet, the Osiris, the scribe Ani, true of voice before Osiris.
sentences.n: ii·n·f 'he has come' is the walking legs with two reeds ii, a reed as complement, n and ·f: the sḏm·n·f, as in part 2. tꜣ pn 'this land' has the same curled earth sign as line 128 (coded N16, approximate), with pn 'this', p and n, after it. iṯ·n·f 'he has taken' is a cord on a small legged support (coded V13, approximate), read iṯ, with walking legs, t, the low sign U15, n and ·f, as part 2 writes iṯt 'take'; the t is taken as a complement, ṯ and t having fallen together in speech. No object is written, and 'it', the land, is supplied. rdwy·f 'his two feet' is r and d with two legs and walking legs as classifiers, and ·f (Budge's numeral 132 is printed between the legs): to take land with one's feet is to walk into it and hold it. The subject is named after the verbs: wsir sš ꜣny mꜣꜥ-ḫrw, with the low seat for wsir and no sickle in mꜣꜥ-ḫrw, as in part 4; ḫr wsir 'before Osiris' is the placenta ḫ and r, and wsir in full. Line 132 begins with wsir.

sentences.n: ntf 'he' is the independent pronoun, n, t and f: ntf N, 'he is N', a sentence without a verb, like ink N 'I am N'. tm 'Atum' as in line 130. iw·f m niwt·k 'he is in your town': iw·f with a prepositional phrase. niwt 'town' is the crossroads in a circle with t and a stroke, and ·k. glossary.wꜥb: wꜥb — to be pure, clean; to purify oneself, bathe (verb); pure (adjective) · also wꜥb 'wab-priest', the 'pure one', a priest of the ordinary rank (noun) · also wꜥb 'purification, purity' (noun) · also wꜥbt 'the pure place', the place of embalming (noun f.)
glossary.msqt: msqt — the Meseqet, a place in the world below (place name; meaning of the name not clear; Budge: Mesqet)
glossary.inpw: inpw — Anubis, the jackal god of the cemetery and of embalming (god's name; Budge: Ànpu)
glossary.iw: iw — opens a statement, often with a suffix (iw·f "he …"); not translated (particle)
glossary.m-sꜣ: m-sꜣ — behind, after (compound preposition: m 'in' + sꜣ 'back')
glossary.ꜥfdt: ꜥfdt — chest, box (noun f.; Budge: āfṭet)
glossary.nty: nty — who, which, that (relative adjective); as a noun "he who"
glossary.ẖr: ẖr — under; also carrying, holding (preposition; Budge: χer)
glossary.wsir: wsir — Osiris, god of the dead and king of the world below; Wsir N "the Osiris N", the dead person (god's name; Budge: Àusàr)
glossary.rdi: rdi — to give, put, place; with a sḏm·f, to cause, let (verb; di·f pr·i "he let me come forth")
glossary.ky: ky — other, another (adjective; ky ḏd 'another saying', which brings in a variant explanation)
glossary.ḏd: ḏd — to say, speak (verb; ḏd in N "said by N", the formula that brings in a speech); ḏdt "words, speech" (noun from it)
glossary.tꜣ: tꜣ — to be hot; tꜣ-ib 'hot-tempered' · a second word of the same spelling: land, earth (noun; plural tꜣw 'lands'; dual tꜣwy 'the Two Lands', Egypt; tp tꜣ 'upon earth')
glossary.qnqn: qnqn — to beat, strike (verb); the beating (?) (noun; Budge: qenqen)
glossary.šw: šw — empty, lacking, free (of) (adjective; verb šwi 'be empty') · a second word of the same spelling: Shu, god of the air, who holds up the sky (god's name; Budge: Śu)
glossary.irt: irt — eye (noun f.; dual irty 'the two eyes')
glossary.ḥr: ḥr — face; (preposition) upon, on, over, concerning · a second word of the same spelling: Horus, the falcon god, son of Osiris and Isis; the sun as a falcon (god's name; Budge: Ḥeru) · also 'at' (ḥr sbꜣw 'at the gates'); ḥr-tp 'upon' (compound preposition: ḥr + tp 'head') · also for, on behalf of; on account of (preposition; ḥr·k 'for you')
glossary.smꜣt: smꜣt — place of union (?) (noun f.; from smꜣ 'unite'; perhaps the tomb; Budge: samat)
glossary.qd: qd — to build (verb; written with the man building a wall; Budge: qeṭ)
glossary.pr: pr — comes forth, 'who comes forth' (participle of pri, to go/come out) · a second word of the same spelling: the noun pr "house, temple, domain" (pr wsir "the house of Osiris"); the verb itself is filed under pri
glossary.·k: ·k — you, your (2nd person masculine singular suffix pronoun; the basket sign)
glossary.itm: itm — Atum, 'the Complete One', the creator god of Heliopolis (god's name; Budge: Tem)
glossary.snṯ: snṯ — to found, lay out (a building) (verb; also written snt, with t for ṯ; Budge: sent)
glossary.rwti: rwti — the 'Double Lion' (Shu and Tefnut), the 6th assessor god (Budge: Rereti)
glossary.pḥ: pḥ — to reach, arrive at, attain (verb)
glossary.sḏm·n·f: sḏm·n·f — the n of the sḏm·n·f, marking a completed action ("I have …", "I …ed") (verb form; written between the verb and its suffix)
glossary.rrt: rrt — a mineral substance, medicine or powder (?) (noun f.; the word is not otherwise known; Budge: rert)
glossary.twr: twr — to be clean, pure; to cleanse, purify (verb)
glossary.nṯri: nṯri — to be divine (?) (verb of quality)
glossary.stẖ: stẖ — Seth, god of storm and disorder, who murdered Osiris (god's name; written stẖ or swt; Budge: Sut)
glossary.ṯs-pẖr: ṯs-pẖr — and vice versa, conversely (adverbial phrase, closing a statement that holds both ways; how it is built is not sure, ṯs perhaps 'saying' + pẖr 'turn round'; Budge: θes rer)
glossary.ii: ii — to come (verb; ii·n·i "I have come")
glossary.pn: pn — this (masculine demonstrative, after its noun)
glossary.iṯi: iṯi — to take, seize, take possession of (verb 3ae-inf; participle iṯ 'who took')
glossary.rd: rd — foot, leg (noun; dual rd·fy "his two feet") · a second word of the same spelling: to grow (verb)
glossary.sš: sš — scribe (noun; the palette-and-pen sign) · a second word of the same spelling: to pass, go through (verb; doubtful here) · also to write, draw, paint (verb; written with the scribe's palette) · also the noun 'writing, document, record' (noun m.) · also to open (a door), spread open (verb; said of doors and bolts) · a further word of the same spelling: nest (noun m.; written with the nest of young birds; dual sšwy)
glossary.ꜣny: ꜣny — Ani, royal scribe of Thebes, for whom the papyrus was made (personal name)
glossary.mꜣꜥ-ḫrw: mꜣꜥ-ḫrw — true of voice, vindicated (epithet; said of the dead whose words were found true at the judgement) · also, as a noun, vindication, the being found true (m mꜣꜥ-ḫrw 'in vindication'; written in full or short)
glossary.ḫr: ḫr — to fall (verb) · a second word of the same spelling: to, near, with (preposition; of persons) · also 'before' (ḫr nṯrw 'before the gods')
glossary.ntf: ntf — he (3rd person masculine singular independent pronoun; ntf N 'he is N', a sentence without a verb)
